content_text_body:
* For many of us, this meeting may be taking place remotely at this time.  If available, turn on cameras so you can see how people are responding and engaging in the discussion. Make sure that whatever video conferencing system you are using is working properly.

* If at all possible, make an extra effort to ensure that you have chosen a time that allows everyone in the team to join, participate and focus on the discussion.

* Have the discussion soon after the survey results are available, when it is fresh and relevant for people.  This is especially important now, when events are moving quickly.

* At the start of the team meeting, first explain that this is not a usual survey because we are in exceptional circumstances.  We are going to use everyone's feedback to find out how we can help and support one another. Acknowledge that the situation is dynamic and it is not possible for anyone to have all the answers - we are moving forward flexibly.

* Individual circumstances might be uniquely impacted at this time - so acknowledge that this is not the forum to address issues that only affect us individually - these can be addressed in upcoming 1:1s.  Instead, this discussion is intended to enable the team to work on things that affect the group.

* The 'Executive Summary Report' is a great overview of the results; use that in the team meeting to get the conversation going and ask probing questions to get a deeper understanding.

* Acknowledge and emphasize the areas where the feedback is positive.  Identify what you and/or your team is doing well. Commit to continuing to do those things well as a team and use them as role models to tackle challenges.

* Reflecting on the areas of concern you identified in Action 3, share where scores are lowest or comments (if available) are most concerning. Help your team get to the root causes of negative experiences or concerns in those areas. If you find the conversation getting too negative, steer it by asking for suggestions on how to improve.

* Encourage open, honest dialogue about what could be improved and focus on how the team can all help one another.

* Remember, it's all about two-way conversation - the survey is just there to get you started! Have follow-up conversations with your team to find out more about what they have expressed in the survey. This should not be just a one-time conversation. The best way to prioritize this is to add it as a standing agenda item in your meetings (both with the wider team and 1:1s).
